issues.reason: A bare-kind (mass) subject with a verbal predicate is a generic, which Quantifiers, generics & scope turns into a distributing `(Implication (Member $x mire_essence) ...)` rule, and Propositional attitudes requires the seal to carry 'P's full normalized form' — so the flat event is the wrong form (though, being tenseless, it reads as habitual by the status default rather than as the specific occurrence the reviewer describes), and it neither distributes nor matches the rule form the parse's own third seal uses.

Detaching the restriction widens the sealed claim from salt-bloom-bearing essence to mire-essence at large and additionally posits of the kind that mire-essence carries salt-bloom, which Core patterns bars in terms — 'a stated restriction, hedge or qualifier is never silently dropped: omitting it widens the claim — carry it, or leave the whole claim out and record the gap'.

The seal-projection table lets exactly three things out of an attitude seal — `Member`/`Name` typing, compound-kind decomposition, and a factive's P — and says outright that 'a referent's possessor / Of links stated only inside P stay sealed'; `tell` is non-factive, so the of-phrase link belongs inside the sealed `(And ...)`, not beside it.

gaps_confirmed: A PP-restricted kind subject in a generic ('mire-essence with salt-bloom burns slowly') — the adjectivally-restricted-kind-subject rule routes the restriction into a premise conjunct but names no head for a PP restriction, and no rule licenses a surface preposition on a kind symbol.

A rate/degree PP on an event ('burning at full rate') — it answers none of where/when/how-manner/whence/whither and is not an aboutness PP, while 'a degree adverb on a verb' is explicitly slotless, so nothing selects the preposition-named `(At ...)` the parse used; that improvisation is nonetheless true and well-typed, so it is a gap, not a defect.
new_gaps: No licensed form exists for the first told proposition: a compliant one would need a head that restricts a kind — or the rule's premise variable — by a PP, e.g. a premise conjunct `(With $x salt_bloom)` beside `(Member $x mire_essence)`, or a condition slot for verbal generics parallel to `ConditionalProperty`, so the restriction rides the burning claim instead of standing beside it as an independent kind-level atom.

A sealed generic has no truth-value carrier: an `(Implication ...)` nested as a term argument of `Theme` cannot carry the (STV 0.9 0.9) a generic requires, so a reported regularity and a reported certainty seal identically; the seal grammar registers the no-polarity-inside-a-seal limitation but not this no-STV one.
A non-Gregorian day-count date ('day 590 of Year 2') has no term: `(Day <n>)` is the day-of-month slot, so a day-of-year ordinal (590) silently reuses a slot that means something else.
defect_summary: Issue 0's compliant form is the distributing rule sealed as the `Theme` conjunct — `(Implication (And (Member $x mire_essence) <restriction>) (And (Member (sk_burn $x) burn) (Patient (sk_burn $x) $x) (Manner (sk_burn $x) slowly)))` — in place of the flat burn event. Issue 1 has NO licensed compliant form: no head can restrict a kind or a rule variable by a PP, so the only licensed move is Core patterns' own fallback — leave the whole claim out and record the gap (filed above). Issue 2's compliant form keeps `(PartOf sk_lantern_1 northcove)` inside the sealed `(And ...)`, leaving only the `GroupOf`/`Member`/`Name` typing and the compound-kind decomposition atoms at top level.
notes: The attitude routing itself is right and the reviewer's read of it matches mine — non-factive `tell` with `Experiencer` holder and `Recipient` addressee, no predication of P at top level, seal-internal indefinites kept sealed, and the indefinite-subject witness in the fourth seal correctly not a rule. All three confirmed issues concern what goes inside versus beside a seal, and two of them have no fully licensed replacement.
